title: To Manipulate or Not: Opinion Dynamics in LLM Interactions
abstract: arXiv:2610.28875v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models increasingly take part in extended conversations where they can both shape and be shaped by another party's views, yet most persuasion research measures only one side of that exchange. We introduce a controlled LLM-LLM debate framework in which two language-model roles repeatedly discuss a contested topic (climate-change attribution): one is given an assigned stance and, in some conditions, an explicit instruction to persuade, while the other receives no assigned position. Across four ordered model combinations involving GPT-6 Luna and Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite, we track both each role's explicitly reported position and a separate measure of its turn-by-turn behavior inside the conversation. Opinion dynamics differ substantially across model combinations: same-model interactions narrow the opinion gap on average, clearly for only one of the two models, while cross-model interactions widen it. translated_title: 操纵与否：大语言模型交互中的观点动态
translated_abstract: 大语言模型越来越多地参与到长时间的对话中，在这些对话里它们既能塑造对方的观点，也会被对方的观点所影响，然而大多数说服研究只测量了这种交流的单个方面。我们提出了一个受控的LLM-LLM辩论框架，其中两个语言模型角色围绕一个有争议的话题（气候变化的归因）反复展开讨论：其中一个角色被赋予指定立场，并且在某些条件下还会收到明确的说服指令，而另一个角色则没有被指定任何立场。在涉及GPT-6 Luna和Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite的四种有序模型组合中，我们同时追踪了每个角色明确报告的立场，以及对其在对话中逐轮言行的独立测量。不同模型组合下的观点动态存在显著差异：同模型交互平均而言会缩小观点差距（且明显地仅对两个模型中的一个成立），而跨模型交互则会扩大观点差距。明确报告与内部……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究提出受控的LLM-LLM辩论框架并同时追踪显式立场与逐轮行为，发现同模型交互倾向于缩小观点差距而跨模型交互则扩大差距，揭示了不同模型间说服动态的显著差异。
en_tdlr: Introducing a controlled LLM-LLM debate framework that tracks both explicit stances and turn-by-turn behavior, this study finds that same-model interactions narrow opinion gaps while cross-model interactions widen them.
